required_inputs.fail_closed: No invented recipient, no decryption key in Actions/source/target, no encryption success claimed from a ciphertext checksum alone.

batches.name: Freeze executable boundary and dispatch feasibility
batches.minimum_change: Extend the already registered deploy-vps.yml workflow on a reviewed non-main ref. Add explicit legacy-publish, legacy-recovery, legacy-activate and legacy-rollback operation branches. Existing host-preflight stays read-only and existing release defaults/gates stay unchanged. No new workflow registration through main.
gates: All legacy branches require workflow_dispatch, exact operation, same-repository non-main protected ref, frozen workflow SHA, bootstrap ID and approved-plan hash; reject main/PR/push/unrecognized operations.
Only legacy-recovery/activate/rollback can request production Secrets/environment approval. legacy-publish receives no VPS or database Secrets.
Use the existing deploy-vps concurrency group across bootstrap and normal deploy; do not cancel a running maintenance job. Remote phases also require a scoped host lock and re-observation.

Before first dispatch, verify the default branch still contains workflow_dispatch, the selected ref's operation inputs are accepted by API, environment branch restrictions permit that ref, and actual run headSha/event/jobs match the frozen request.
Use a non-privileged fixture dispatch first: no source SSH, production Secrets, registry publish, or target writes; reject any unexpected normal release/deploy job.
acceptance: Dispatch matrix and malformed-input tests pass; existing main release semantics are preserved.
Coordinator retains API/run identity and independent review; HTTP dispatch acceptance alone is not execution evidence.

batches.name: Publish a truthfully signed old-source runner and builder
batches.minimum_change: A source-only legacy-publish job builds runner and builder from an untouched git archive of the operator-confirmed old commit, publishes host-matching immutable GHCR digests, signs both digests and a deterministic public materials manifest with the real workflow identity.
gates: Record old_commit, old_git_tree, archive_sha256, extracted file/mode/hash manifest, Dockerfile/lock/.dockerignore hashes, git archive export-attribute exclusions, platform, resolved base/dependency materials, runner/builder config IDs and OCI digests.

Build file/context both point inside the archived old tree. Labels/build arguments are external build metadata; no candidate files, npm edits, dependency upgrades, source patch or injected runtime files enter that context.
record live_legacy_image_id and newly_built_old_image_id separately; equality is not assumed. Same-source rebuild is not a byte-for-byte legacy daemon attestation.

Signer workflow/source SHA is the actual reviewed non-main GitHub run SHA, not old_commit. Verify repository, exact signer workflow path, signer digest, source digest/ref and subject digest with official gh verification.

Sign the public materials manifest as a file subject in the same workflow, then verify its file hash/signature and independently recompute the old commit/tree/archive linkage from Git. A custom unverified predicate is not sufficient.

Reject wrong workflow, wrong workflow SHA, wrong old tree/archive, tampered signed manifest and swapped runner/builder digest. A negative test using old_commit as stock --source-digest must reject when the workflow runs at a newer SHA.
Keep publication permissions to contents:read, packages:write, id-token:write and attestations:write in the publication job; no production environment Secret inheritance.
acceptance: Both OCI subjects and materials file have real verifiable bundles, exact digest pulls succeed, negative controls fail, and host platform is supported.
Publisher tooling/actions are pinned to reviewed immutable versions; no reproducible-build claim is made for floating historical bases or package repositories.

batches.name: Implement and fixture-test consistent recovery, encryption and reliable transfer
batches.minimum_change: Create a dedicated legacy recovery mode; leave scripts/test/rehearse-release.sh candidate UID gate untouched. First test only generated fixture data and an isolated local target receiver; real execution remains separately approved.
gates: Fixture tests cover same-snapshot inventory versus restored inventory, pg_dump/restore errors, insufficient space, wrong live identity, live-volume/network alias refusal, interrupted transfer, tampered ciphertext, receiver path traversal/symlink attempts, stale or mismatched evidence, and cleanup.
Legacy root exemption is limited to bootstrap-confirmed old digests and exact original local image ID; record UID 0 and expiry. It cannot enable a root candidate release.
No normal rehearsal rollback-approved marker or candidate previous-env is created by this mode.
Existing-password positive/negative TCP authentication check is performed without Secret values, auth hashes or connection strings in logs.
acceptance: Independent cross-family Evaluator tests the scripts and evidence parser from a clean checkout with fixture data, not the Planner's narration.
No scripts can emit raw dumps, raw configs, cookies or real credentials to an artifact/log destination; redaction and artifact traversal tests cover refusal paths.

batches.name: Separately approved real recovery and exact legacy fallback retention
batches.minimum_change: Execute only the reviewed legacy-recovery operation through protected Actions source transport. Preserve actual legacy app/image/config; dump the real source with a common snapshot, restore only isolated PG16, run old and exact legacy scratch canaries, encrypt and deliver ciphertext, then obtain offline decrypt/restore confirmation.
gates: Source and target identity/capacity/approved path observations are current and match the frozen plan. No broader host inventory or unrelated credential search.
Original app stays serving throughout recovery; no production schema mutation, postgres restart, live restore or .env overwrite.
Plaintext dump and configs remain restricted on source; ciphertext is the only backup material permitted on runner/target, and no backup bytes are uploaded to Actions artifacts.
Remote durable receipt and offline decrypt/restore receipt are both verified and tied to the exact ciphertext/plaintext hashes and bootstrap ID.
Retain exact daemon image ID via a bootstrap-specific local tag and restricted docker save archive; retain original env/Compose files with mode/hash metadata, outside rsync --delete reach.
Rehearse fallback app-only recreation against scratch using retained exact image and config semantics, then recheck source app/image/DB identity before permitting activation.
acceptance: Real snapshot inventory equals restored inventory; old migration is scratch-only and leaves inventory unchanged; old digest and original legacy-image enroll/ingest/summary canaries clean up exactly.
Evidence says real-production-data, not synthetic; no secret values/dump bytes leave private storage or appear in public artifacts.
Backup age, rollback horizon, source/target receipt and independent review meet approved limits; otherwise activation remains refused.

batches.name: Gated app-only baseline activation and operational rollback
batches.minimum_change: Activate only the verified old-source digest runner against the unchanged existing DB/project/backend with a reviewed env and app-only Compose override. Run no live migration, build or database service operation. Publish baseline activation ledger only after observation.
gates: Complete the activation/rollback fixture tests and fresh cross-family evaluation of their exact implementation SHA before any real activation; P3 recovery success does not waive this implementation gate.

All real recovery and cryptographic material evidence is verified, recent, immutable, tied to source/image/plan, and independently accepted; human environment approval is granted for this exact operation.
Dry-resolved Compose proves existing project/network/volume/backend and same secrets/password semantics; no candidate/new migrations or config leak. Sanitize ambient Compose/Docker/proxy overrides.

The only live replacement is app with --no-deps --no-build --pull never after exact digest verification/pull. No up postgres, migrate, rsync --delete, source rebuild, image/volume prune or password change.
Immediately before replacement, assert original serving container/image/project/port/DB identity and host lock still match; otherwise no-op refusal.
Observe new container .Image equals verified old digest config ID, old health SHA matches, read-only business/session/browser checks pass, and postgres container/start/volume identity is unchanged.

Failure triggers bounded bootstrap-specific rollback of app only from the retained local exact image/config with --no-deps --no-build --pull never; no automatic DB restore. If fallback readiness fails, contain the app, retain evidence and escalate.
acceptance: Write .releases/<old_sha>.manifest and .activated only from verified immutable digests and observed serving activation; no pre-created ledger, fabricated previous-env or rollback-approved gate.
Use immutable no-replace writes; preexisting mismatched files refuse instead of overwrite. Keep bootstrap recovery/config ledger separate from candidate evidence.
Independent observer verifies local/public old SHA, serving digest and read-only flow; this is baseline acceptance, not candidate or F005/Agent signoff.

batches.name: Hand off eligible predecessor, not a release verdict
batches.minimum_change: Coordinator retains signed public baseline materials, redacted real recovery/activation receipts and private custody locations. Later exact-candidate release must pass its own native/DB/browser/OCI/provenance/live recovery and human gates.
gates: Rerun existing verify-vps-predecessor.sh read-only with the future distinct candidate to prove guard compatibility; do not fabricate its output or mutate a ledger to pass.
POSTGRES_PASSWORD is present at the correct protected environment scope and positive/negative authentication was verified against the actual persisted role without rotation.
Current candidate Windows failures and pending independent evaluation remain release blockers. Main-only candidate provenance is not replaced by the non-main old-source publisher.

Future candidate previous-env is copied from the observed activated baseline at the normal candidate boundary; candidate live-dump/scratch/migrated-old rollback proof and rollback-approved marker are generated anew.
Agent manifest pin and F005 real logged-in 65-second freshness acceptance remain separate and cannot be claimed by this maintenance operation.
acceptance: Coordinator alone transports reviewed implementation and decides the subsequent permitted push; workers never push.
Any expired/changed source, digest, workflow, secret policy, retention, schema or candidate SHA reopens the relevant gate.

consistent_recovery_contract.source: Exactly the inventory-approved database/container/project; role/database and live volume IDs are explicit inputs, not guessed aliases.
consistent_recovery_contract.snapshot: Keep one READ ONLY REPEATABLE READ transaction open; export its snapshot, record inventory in that transaction, and invoke pg_dump -Fc --no-owner --snapshot=<that snapshot> in the same database while the exporter remains alive. No post-dump live inventory equality assertion under continuing writes.
private_inventory: database identity/version and source volume ID
row counts for every old-schema critical model, including User/Device/Project/UsageEvent and credential/session tables
approved min/max occurrence timestamps and referential orphan counts
consistent_recovery_contract.restore: Require source PostgreSQL major 16 and compatible pinned dump/restore client versions; a different or unknown major needs a revised compatibility spec. Hash and check a completed private dump. Restore with pg_restore --exit-on-error --no-owner into a pinned PG16 image on a unique internal-only network and scratch-only fresh volume, with no host port and no live mount. Compare inventory before any migrations or canary.
consistent_recovery_contract.scratch_app: Use synthetic scratch-only Auth/admin/mail/session secrets, disable optional outbound activity and prevent egress. Run old builder migration only on scratch, then old digest runner and retained exact original runner canaries with the old generated Prisma client and reviewed mounted canary harness.
consistent_recovery_contract.canary: Create one scratch-only synthetic identity, enroll device, ingest one event, verify authenticated summary and one stored row, delete identity and dependent data, compare full inventory again. Never run this write canary on production.
consistent_recovery_contract.cleanup: Remove only resource IDs created and recorded by this bootstrap. Keep failed evidence and approved recoverable backups; no broad Docker prune, live restore or assumption that deleting files securely erases their blocks. Record cleanup outcome.
consistent_recovery_contract.freshness: Approved recovery-point age and rollback expiry are mandatory. If live writes continue between dump and activation, report measured age/RPO; do not claim zero data loss or identical live counts. Refresh recovery after expiry.

minimum_inputs: operator-supplied age public recipient and verified fingerprint
separate operator-controlled isolated decrypt/PG16 restore host
choices.constraints: Use reviewed/version-pinned age recipient encryption only. Do not generate or export an identity in Actions, use an SSH private key as recipient, or place private keys on source/dmitsvr. No passphrase mode or fallback on missing recipient.

minimum_inputs: verified full public-key fingerprint and valid encryption subkey
choices.constraints: Encrypt to the exact verified nonexpired/revoked public recipient; no public-server discovery by name, private-key import or unattended passphrase in CI. Requires separately reviewed pinned tooling and fixture tests. Choose one scheme; do not implement both by default.

encrypted_offhost_contract.transport: Recommended narrow path: source encrypts the real dump in restricted storage, existing approved Actions source SSH reads only ciphertext into a private ephemeral runner file without logging it, and the runner transfers only ciphertext to dmitsvr using a newly authorized dedicated upload-only target identity. The local dmitsvr alias private key is never copied into CI, reused, or forwarded. No agent forwarding.
encrypted_offhost_contract.target_auth: Target owner provisions a new restricted account/credential after separate approval. Forced receiver command, no shell/PTY/forwarding/arbitrary paths/read/delete. New upload private credential is a short-lived protected Actions authentication Secret, not an encryption/decryption identity; only recovery job receives it. Revoke after the approved upload horizon. If operator declines this new credential, stop and request a separately specified transfer mechanism.
encrypted_offhost_contract.trust: Source and target public host fingerprints must be independently pinned. ssh-keyscan output alone is trust discovery, not verification; no StrictHostKeyChecking=no or TOFU-only success claim.
encrypted_offhost_contract.receiver: Only approved child of /var/backups, owned by designated receiver with mode 0700; files 0600. Validate bootstrap ID/basename/size/hash, reject traversal/symlinks and overwrites. Write .partial, fsync file, verify full ciphertext SHA256/size, atomic no-replace rename on same filesystem, fsync parent, then return bounded hash/size/receipt ID. Existing complete identical file permits idempotent receipt; mismatch refuses.
encrypted_offhost_contract.retry: At most the approved bounded retries of the same frozen ciphertext, never a new dump or recipient. Interrupted .partial is not complete; owner-scoped cleanup/expiry only. A transport exit zero is insufficient without post-write durable receipt and hash comparison.
encrypted_offhost_contract.decrypt_restore: Custodian obtains ciphertext and signed/redacted receipt from dmitsvr through their own authorized access, verifies ciphertext, decrypts outside Actions/source/target, verifies plaintext dump hash and restores isolated PG16. Return only signed or otherwise owner-authenticated redacted receipt bound to bootstrap ID, recipient fingerprint, hashes, inventory result and cleanup. No decrypt key or plaintext is returned to CI.
encrypted_offhost_contract.retention: User approves exact source plaintext expiry, original image/config horizon, target ciphertext expiry and immutable rollback window. Preserve at least one decrypt-and-restore-confirmed recovery point. Target/operator performs deletion; upload account cannot prune backups. Unknown capacity/expiry/custody refuses activation.

password_contract.intent: Verify and safely set the existing persisted PostgreSQL role password, never rotate it.
password_contract.proof: On the inventory-approved source, a temporary client uses the candidate existing value through protected stdin and a 0600 pgpass file. Require TCP positive authentication and SELECT of expected database/current_user; require same-path fresh randomized wrong password to fail. Reject trust/peer/socket-only or ambiguous authentication. Output booleans and scoped identity only; remove temporary credentials.
password_contract.preferred_set: Authorized human Secret owner supplies the existing value from their approved custody via gh secret set POSTGRES_PASSWORD --env production reading protected stdin, or the official GitHub Secret UI. Never --body with a plaintext argv value, shell history, chat, logs, clipboard export or a tracked .env. Name-list/API verification proves only presence; protected connection test proves usability.
password_contract.value_unavailable: Do not export a password merely because Actions can SSH. If only source protected config holds it, stop for an explicit one-shot sealed GitHub-public-key bridge design/approval: source verifies locally and seals the selected password to the exact production environment Secrets public key; CI sees only sealed ciphertext and a short-lived least-privilege Secret-writer token submits only POSTGRES_PASSWORD. Official API permissions/sealed-box helper must be verified before this optional mechanism is implemented. No administrator PAT borrowed from local stores.
password_contract.existing_representation: Current deploy validation requires URL-unreserved single-line password bytes. If the real password is incompatible, stop and propose a separately reviewed quoting/URL-encoding change; do not silently change it to satisfy the regex.
prohibitions: recreating or restarting postgres to apply env
assuming POSTGRES_PASSWORD env changes an existing cluster role
printing Config.Env, full docker compose config, .env, auth hashes or password hashes
password_contract.scope: Setting GitHub Secret is an operator action under separate Secret-owner approval, not a Planner/Generator task or part of this proposal execution.

never_actions_artifact: original/baseline/previous env or resolved Compose config
database URLs, bearer/session/canary tokens, credentials, private keys
pgpass or raw command stderr/response bodies
real-data logs/traces or unrestricted directory uploads
artifact_policy.publication_policy: Stage only regular explicitly named validated bounded files; reject symlinks, extra files, path escape and unknown JSON keys. Round-trip retained evidence and compare manifest/hash/signature. Signed JSON is evidence only after verification, not instructions.
artifact_policy.private_source: Approved backup root with 0700 directory/0600 files; original env/config/image archive, snapshot inventory and plaintext dump stay private with explicit retention.
artifact_policy.private_target: Approved 0700 target backup child holds ciphertext and bounded receipt only; no source environment or decryption key.
evidence_fields: original and activated app image/container IDs
remote durable receipt and offline decrypt/restore receipt hashes
artifact_policy.absent_evidence: Use null/unknown/refused and a fixed reason code; never backfill an observed, activated, restored or approved fact from the plan.

before_cutover: scoped read-only Docker/image/Compose/network/volume identity and bounded local health queries
read-only PostgreSQL snapshot/export/inventory and custom-format dump clients
scratch-only network/volume/container creation, restore/migration/canary and exact recorded cleanup
digest pulls and offline attestation/material verification
restricted backup/config snapshot, encryption and approved ciphertext transfer
cutover: bounded readiness and approved read-only business observation
rollback: recreate only legacy app from exact retained image and original config using --no-deps --no-build --pull never
bounded old-health/image/business observation and immutable incident receipt
always_forbidden: source/target env or backup upload to Actions artifacts

remote_path_and_identity_allowlist.source_deploy_root: Only the canonical non-symlink VPS_DEPLOY_PATH authenticated by source inventory; currently null/unverified. Within it, read .env, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.release.yml and exactly named .releases/<sha>.manifest/.activated/.previous-env. Source-material hashing covers only archive-manifest-listed build inputs within this root, not home directories or unrelated deployments.
remote_path_and_identity_allowlist.source_private_root: Only a separately approved canonical backup root outside deployment sync and its bootstrap_id child; currently null/unverified. Fixed private basenames: original.env, original-compose.yml, original-release-compose.yml, original-image.tar, snapshot-inventory.json, database.dump, database.dump.sha256, database.dump.age OR database.dump.gpg, recovery-private.json, baseline.env, app-only-override.yml. Temporary names have only the approved .partial suffix.
remote_path_and_identity_allowlist.target_private_root: Proposed /var/backups/tokenizer-bootstrap/<bootstrap_id>, not an observed/created directory. Target owner must approve/create the 0700 parent child and receiver ownership. Only database.dump.age OR database.dump.gpg, its .partial file and bounded receipt.json are writable; all other target paths refuse.
remote_path_and_identity_allowlist.docker_scope: Only inventory-approved serving app/postgres IDs, their exact image IDs and source network/volume; newly created bootstrap scratch IDs use a frozen tokenizer-bootstrap-<bootstrap_id>- prefix. Operations refuse labels or IDs outside those sets. No enumeration of other projects to discover a substitute.
remote_path_and_identity_allowlist.host_identity: Only approved source/target public SSH fingerprints and bounded opaque hashes of machine/failure-domain identity supplied by operator or a reviewed fixed identity query. A distinct fingerprint/host ID is necessary but insufficient for independent storage/failure-domain proof; require an explicit operator statement.
remote_path_and_identity_allowlist.input_safety: bootstrap_id is a bounded lowercase alphanumeric/hyphen identifier, SHAs/digests are strict fixed-width hex, all roots are canonical absolute non-symlink paths, argv is fixed and not eval/source, and all shell interpolation/ambient overrides are rejected or sanitized. Unknown IDs/roots never default to a guess.

planner_local_checks: unique input/batch IDs and dependency references
only the two delivery files changed
verification_and_handoff.independent_execution: All implementation and real-execution evidence needs fresh cross-family evaluation, exact-SHA CI and appropriate user/operator approvals. This supporting proposal is not an Evaluator verdict.
verification_and_handoff.current_go_no_go: NO_GO: required source/material, recipient/custody, target transport, real recovery, existing password verification and exact-candidate Windows/evaluator gates are unclosed.
